Modern Faber

A Letter to Builders

For people who ship Read slowly

Manifesto

Most groups talk.

They share links.
They debate ideas.
They orbit around the idea of doing something meaningful.

Nothing gets built.

We are not that.

We believe in a different standard.

Not intelligence as abstraction, but as execution.
Not taste as opinion, but as decisions made under constraint.
Not ambition as narrative, but as output—visible, undeniable, shipped.

We care about what exists because you made it.

This is a room for people who build.

People who obsess over details no one else notices.
Who rework something ten times when once would suffice.
Who feel discomfort when something is “almost right.”

Craft is not a claim here.
It is evidence.

We are not interested in volume.

We are interested in consistency.

Showing up, every week, with something real.
Something you struggled through.
Something unfinished but undeniable.

Not once.
Not occasionally.

Every week.

This is not a place to consume.

It is a place to produce.

You will be seen through your work.
You will be challenged on your decisions.
You will be measured by what you do, not what you say.

And in return—

You will be surrounded by others doing the same.

There is no audience here.

Only participants.

If you are looking for validation, this will feel uncomfortable.
If you are looking for growth, it will feel inevitable.

Over time, something happens.

A body of work emerges.
A standard sharpens.
A network forms—not through introductions, but through proof.

A map gets drawn, one point at a time.

This is a simple system.

Show up.
Build something real.
Do it again next week.

Internal Operating Policy

Community Policy

Craft Group exists to enforce a weekly standard. If meaningful work is not shipping, the system is failing.

  1. 01

    Objective

    This group is designed to produce consistent, high-quality output through enforced accountability.

    Everything optimizes for one outcome: members ship meaningful work every week. If this is not happening, the system is failing.

  2. 02

    Operating Principles

    1. Output is the only signal that matters.
    2. Consistency beats intensity.
    3. Constraints create quality.
    4. Social pressure is a feature, not a bug.
    5. Removal is necessary to maintain standards.
  3. 03

    System Design (Non-Negotiable)

    Weekly cadence is fixed. There is no rolling submission window.

    • Fixed weekly deadline.
    • All submissions posted before deadline.
    • No batching and no skipping weeks.

    Submission format is strict and non-negotiable.

    • [Output]
      • Link.
      • 1–3 line description.
    • [Craft]
      • What specific detail was iterated on and why.
    • [Blocker]
      • Where progress slowed or failed.

    No deviation from format.

  4. 04

    Enforcement Mechanism

    This group survives on enforcement.

    • 2 consecutive missed submissions leads to removal.
    • 3 total misses, even if non-consecutive, leads to removal.
    • Repeated low-effort output leads to removal.
    • No engagement, including no comments or feedback, leads to removal.

    No exceptions.

    Low effort includes the following:

    • No meaningful progress since the last submission.
    • Superficial updates that are cosmetic or trivial.
    • Recycled or old work.

    Judgment is made by the operator.

  5. 05

    Membership Pipeline

    Entry requirements:

    • Proof of recent work from within the last two weeks.
    • Self-initiated work, not assigned work.
    • Clear demonstration of decision-making.

    Screening questions:

    • What did you build recently?
    • What was hard about it?
    • What did you iterate on multiple times?

    Reject fast if the answers are vague.

  6. 06

    Onboarding Protocol

    Before the Slack invite:

    • Review the policy. This is mandatory.
    • Submit an initial work sample.

    During the first week:

    • Submit within the first cycle.
    • Failure to submit results in immediate removal.

    Filter early, not later.

  7. 07

    Slack Structure (Locked)

    Channels:

    • #build for submissions only.
    • #intro for onboarding only.
    • #random for everything else.

    Rules:

    • No discussions in #build beyond feedback.
    • No content dumping in #random.
    • No new channels without approval.
  8. 08

    Feedback Standard

    Feedback must be specific, actionable, and direct.

    Avoid the following:

    • Praise without substance.
    • Generic comments.

    Minimum standard: each member leaves at least one meaningful comment per week.

  9. 09

    Operator Responsibilities

    The group requires active enforcement.

    • Track weekly submissions.
    • Enforce removals without delay.
    • Maintain the standard of output.
    • Admit new members selectively.

    Failure here means group collapse.

  10. 10

    Failure Modes (Watch Closely)

    1. Activity decay. Fix it with stricter enforcement.
    2. Quality dilution. Remove the weakest contributors quickly.
    3. Overgrowth. Cap or slow admissions.
    4. Conversation drift. Redirect to output focus.
  11. 11

    Growth Strategy

    • Start with 3 to 5 high-quality members.
    • Add slowly, one person at a time.
    • Only admit people who raise the bar.

    Do not optimize for size.

  12. 12

    Culture

    • High accountability.
    • Low tolerance for excuses.
    • Respect through output.
    • Quiet intensity over loud participation.
  13. 13

    Core Rule

    If you are not building, you are removed.

    Everything else is secondary.

Membership

Join

Read the standard, bring recent work, and enter ready to submit in the first cycle.

If that excites you, you already understand.
If it doesn’t, this is not for you.

  • Review the policy before you join.
  • Bring proof of recent self-initiated work.
  • Submit in your first week or you are out.
Accept the invitation

Show up with something real. Do it again next week.
